subject: science

concepts.title: Reversible Changes
concepts.definition: A process where the transformation can be undone to return the substance to its original state or form.
concepts.key_idea: The material can be recovered in its initial condition.
question_patterns: Can this change be reversed?
Is folding a paper a reversible change?
Identify if melting ice is a reversible process
Determine if the change in shape of a balloon is reversible
What happens when you unfold a toy aeroplane?

solution_steps.action: identify the initial and final states
solution_steps.explain: Check if the material has undergone a permanent chemical change or just a physical shift.
Determine if an action like unfolding, melting, or cooling can restore the starting material.

concepts.title: Irreversible Changes
concepts.definition: A permanent transformation that results in a new form or substance which cannot be converted back to the original.
concepts.key_idea: The starting material cannot be retrieved after the change.
question_patterns: Why is baking a roti an irreversible change?
Can a burst balloon be restored to its original form?
Is cutting paper an irreversible process?
What kind of change occurs when a candle burns away?
Explain why curdling of milk cannot be undone.

solution_steps.action: examine the nature of the change
solution_steps.explain: Look for signs of new substances like ash, gas, or cooked material.
Verify if any physical process can turn the product back into the reactant.

concepts.title: Thermal Expansion
concepts.definition: The increase in the size or volume of a material, particularly metals, when subjected to heat.
concepts.key_idea: Materials grow larger when they get hot.
question_patterns: How does heating affect the iron ring of a tool?
Why is the metal rim heated before fixing it to a wheel?
What happens to the size of a metal object when it is red-hot?
Explain the process of expansion in solids.
Why does the iron blade become easier to fix after heating?

solution_steps.explain: Heating causes the particles to move and the material to expand.
The ring or rim becomes slightly larger, allowing it to fit over a handle or wheel.

concepts.title: Thermal Contraction
concepts.definition: The reduction in the dimensions of a material as it cools down and loses heat.
concepts.key_idea: Materials shrink back to their original size upon cooling.
question_patterns: What happens when cold water is poured over a hot metal rim?
How does a cooling ring fit tightly on a wooden handle?
Define contraction in the context of fixing tools.
Why does a metal rim shrink on cooling?
Describe the effect of cooling on a heated iron blade.

solution_steps.explain: Removing heat or applying cold water causes the material to lose energy.
As the material shrinks, it grips the internal object tightly.

concepts.title: Changes by Mixing
concepts.definition: Alterations that occur when two or more substances are combined, which may be reversible or irreversible.
concepts.key_idea: Combining substances can create solutions or new products.
question_patterns: Is dissolving salt in water a reversible change?
What change occurs when curd is added to warm milk?
Can we separate salt from water after mixing?
How does mixing affect the properties of substances?
Identify a change caused by mixing two materials.

solution_steps.explain: Determine if they form a simple mixture or react to form something new.
If evaporation or filtration can recover the parts, it is reversible.

concepts.title: Change in Length due to Burning
concepts.definition: Calculating the reduction in the length of an object, like a candle, after it has been burning for a duration.
concepts.key_idea: Burning consumes material, leading to a measurable decrease in length.
question_patterns: Calculate the change in length of a candle
How much length was lost after burning the candle?
Find the difference in candle height before and after lighting it
What is the reduction in length if the initial was ... and final is ...?
Compute the length consumed during the activity

solution_steps.explain: Identify the initial_length of the object before the change.
Identify the final_length of the object after the change.
The difference represents the amount of material lost.

concepts.title: Growth and Weight Increase
concepts.definition: Determining the increase in body mass or weight as a person or organism grows over time.
concepts.key_idea: Growth results in a positive change in mass.
question_patterns: Calculate the weight gain over the year
How much did the weight increase?
Find the difference between current and previous weight
What is the total growth in mass?
Compute the increase in weight as the child grows

solution_steps.explain: Note the current_weight of the individual.
Note the previous_weight from an earlier time.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A candle was 20 cm long. After burning for an hour, its length is 12 cm. Calculate the change in length.
If a candle of 15 units is burnt until only 5 units remain, what is the length consumed?
A student weighed 35 kg last year and weighs 42 kg now. Find the weight gain.
A baby weighed 3 kg at birth and 10 kg at one year. What is the increase in weight?

solution_template.explain: Weight at one year is 10 kg.
